formula.text: Milliliters = fluid ounces × 29.5735. Fluid ounces = milliliters ÷ 29.5735.

howToSteps.name: Read the fluid ounces
howToSteps.text: Find the amount in fl oz on the bottle, the can, or the recipe. Common sizes are 8, 12, 16, and 32 fl oz.

howToSteps.name: Multiply by 29.5735
howToSteps.text: Fluid ounces times 29.5735 gives milliliters. 8 fl oz is 237 ml, 12 fl oz is 355 ml, 16 fl oz is 473 ml.

howToSteps.name: Check US or imperial
howToSteps.text: An American recipe means the US fluid ounce, 29.5735 ml. A British recipe means the imperial fluid ounce, 28.413 ml.

howToSteps.name: Do not swap in weight ounces
howToSteps.text: Fluid ounces are volume. An ounce on a scale is weight. They only match for water, and even then only roughly.

name: Fluid Ounces to Milliliters
title: Fluid Ounces to Milliliters Converter
tutorial: One US fluid ounce is 29.5735 milliliters. The number comes from the US gallon, which is defined as 231 cubic inches, exactly 3.785411784 liters. A gallon holds 128 fluid ounces, so one fluid ounce is 3785.411784 divided by 128, which is 29.5735 ml.

Fluid ounces measure volume, and ounces measure weight, and the shared word causes more confusion than any other pair in the kitchen. A fluid ounce of water weighs about 1.04 ounces, so the two are close for water and only for water. A fluid ounce of honey weighs about 1.5 ounces, and a fluid ounce of flour is not a measurement anyone should trust.

Bottle sizes are where this conversion lives. A 12 fl oz can is 355 ml. A 16 fl oz bottle is 473 ml, which is a pint. A 32 fl oz carton is 946 ml, which is a quart. A 64 fl oz jug is 1.89 liters, which is half a gallon. Once you know the can and the pint, the rest follow.

The imperial fluid ounce is different: 28.413 ml, about 4 percent smaller than the US fluid ounce. A British recipe that says 10 fl oz means 284 ml, not 296 ml. The difference is small for one drink and noticeable across a punch bowl.

Milliliter results on this page show one decimal below 100 ml and round to whole milliliters above that, so 1 fl oz shows as 29.6 ml and 8 fl oz as 237 ml. The exact factor, 29.5735, is in the formula below.
